name: Samuel E. Bassett
tagline: Top rated Criminal Defense attorney in Austin, Texas
education: The University of Texas School of Law
about: With over three decades of experience under his belt, Samuel E. Bassett, partner at Minton, Bassett, Flores & Carsey, P.C., in Austin, Texas, has established himself as a leading attorney primarily focusing on criminal defense. Having practiced both criminal defense and family law, he advocates for clients in cases involving white collar crimes, felonies, homicides, sexual assault, fraud, major drug charges and DWIs. He predominantly serves in the Austin metro area, including Travis, Hays, Williamson and the surrounding counties.

Mr. Bassett graduated with a bachelor's degree in business administration from The University of Texas at Austin in 1985. Before gaining his licensure in 1988, he earned his Juris Doctor from The University of Texas at Austin School of Law. A standout in his field, he is board-certified in criminal law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization – a distinction held by a small percentage of Texas attorneys – recognizing his trial experience and extensive legal knowledge.

Mr. Bassett has earned multiple accolades and awards, reinforcing his reputation as an advocate for criminal defense clients. He won the Presidential Award from the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association. In the years 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2023, he was titled “Lawyer of the Year” by The Best Lawyers in America for his work in the legal domain. Additionally, he was awarded the Ambassador Award by the Austin Criminal Defense Lawyers Association in 2010.

Beyond his professional achievements, Mr. Bassett has left an indelible mark through his community service. From 2004 until 2010, Mr. Bassett served on the State Bar of Texas District Nine Grievance Panel, upholding the ethical standards of the Texas bar. For his work as the chair of the Texas Forensic Science Commission in ensuring high standards of scientific integrity, he was nominated as a finalist for Texan of the Year. Formerly president of the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, he presently serves on the board of the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Educational Institute.
